convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom for the ZPF indicator and depends on two external .mqh libraries (SmoothAlgorithms.mqh for CXMA class and TradeAlgorithms.mqh for trading functions). Custom indicator not available in standard Python libraries.

derived_values.name: min_rates_total - minimum bars for indicator calculation
TimeShiftSec - timeframe duration in seconds
derived_values.used_by: UpSignalTime and DnSignalTime calculation for trade signal timestamping

other_exits: Opposite signal closes existing position: buy signal closes short, sell signal closes long

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MM parameter: negative values are fixed lot size (abs value), positive values are deposit fraction for deal sizing. Default MM=-0.1 means 0.1 lots fixed.

custom_logic_notes: Entry logic reads ZPF indicator buffer 1 at SignalBar and SignalBar+1. Long entry: Value[1]>0 AND Value[0]<=0 (ZPF crosses above zero). Short entry: Value[1]<0 AND Value[0]>=0 (ZPF crosses below zero). BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose booleans gate permission for each direction. Recount flag ensures signal recalculation on first tick or after copy failure. Signal timestamps are set to last bar date plus one timeframe period for trade identification.
python_conversion_notes: ZPF is a custom indicator requiring porting of SmoothAlgorithms.mqh smoothing functions (JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA). The CXMA class and its GetStartBars method must be reimplemented. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose which handle order execution, lot sizing logic (negative MM=fixed lots, positive=deposit fraction), and position management - these must be reimplemented in Python. Signal logic is zero-line crossover on the ZPF custom indicator. Multi-timeframe support (indicator on H4 while EA runs on any chart) requires proper bar synchronization in Python backtesting.
